measures.title: Emergency Services Sales and Use Tax
measures.summary: Asks whether Santa Clara City may impose a local sales and use tax of up to 1.0% on taxable transactions in the city, as authorized by Utah Code 59-12-2402. The money would fund emergency services, including fire protection, ambulance and emergency medical services, and the personnel, equipment, facilities and operating costs for them.
measures.yesMeans: Santa Clara could impose a sales and use tax of up to 1.0% to fund emergency services.
measures.noMeans: Santa Clara would not be authorized to impose this emergency services sales tax.

measures.title: Emergency Services Sales and Use Tax
measures.summary: Asks whether Washington City should impose an additional 0.67% Emergency Services Sales and Use Tax (1.0% total) on taxable sales in the city to fund emergency services such as fire protection, ambulance service and emergency medical response. The ballot states that if it passes, the City Council intends to cut the City portion of property taxes by 50%, subject to Truth-in-Taxation requirements.
measures.yesMeans: Washington City would add a 0.67% emergency services sales tax, for 1.0% in total.
measures.noMeans: Washington City would not add the emergency services sales tax.
